about: How a run an AI finished becomes a workflow every AI can find and run again (src/learned-workflows.mjs). `min_tool_runs` is how many tools must have run and finished in the work before it is kept as a workflow. `same_job_at_least` is how close (0..1, by meaning when the service can embed, else by shared words, as find_workflow measures it) an earlier learned workflow's job must be for this run to improve it rather than start another. `keep_versions` is how many earlier versions a workflow keeps in its own row. `id_prefix` starts every learned workflow's id. `max_input_chars` and `max_outcome_chars` cut how much of each run's input and of what the job delivered the workflow carries in `learned_from`, which every member who finds it can read. `scope_from` names where a finished job says which spaces it was done in (paths read inside the handoff); the learned workflow is shared into each of them, so the people there have it at once. `failed_states` are the result states that mean the work stopped without its result; such work is handed on as open work with the exact wall, at most `max_retries` times for one job, carrying the tool runs it tried (`tried`, the last `max_tried` of them: task id, tool, state and error) so the next AI starts from them. `publish` says whether a learned job's generic shape (src/learned-workflows.mjs publicShape: its tools in order, each run by Trillion with inputs bound to the workflow's own input or an earlier step's result, words only from the tools' public descriptors) is put on the Marketplace by itself once its checks pass (`on`), the id it is kept under (`id_prefix` plus its tools and this account's maker id), how long a value must be before it is taken as an earlier step's result (`min_chained_chars`) and before it is searched for in the shared steps as this job's own value (`min_private_chars`). Every word an AI or a person reads is under `words`.

lifecycle.what: How a workflow an AI learned ages (src/workflows.mjs age, restore): one that no run has used for stale_after_days is marked stale (still found, said to be stale); at archive_after_days it is archived (not listed by find_workflow; describe_workflow and start_workflow still read and run it). Never deleted. A workflow the person pinned (pinned: true on its row) never ages. Every change is kept on the row in lifecycle_log (at most log_most entries, each with the BLAKE3 identity of the row before the change), and restore_workflow undoes the latest one. Use is read from the run cards, newest first, run_pages pages of 200 at most; when the pages end before the archive horizon is reached nothing ages that pass, so a busy account never ages a workflow it only could not see.

words.lifecycle_stale: {workflow_id} has not been used for {days} days.
words.lifecycle_restored: {workflow_id} is back: it is found again and its clock starts now.
words.lifecycle_not_aged: {workflow_id} is not stale or archived, so there is nothing to restore.
words.lifecycle_unreadable: Runs older than the pages read could not be seen, so nothing was aged this time.
words.label: {job}
words.step_do: Run {tool_id} with run_tool. Last time it ran with this input: {input}. Give it this job's own values instead of last time's, and hand back the task_id it returned. When this account cannot run that tool, find_tool_for_job finds one that does the same job.
words.result_do: Say what this job delivered and where the person can see it.
words.learned_note: Trillion kept this job's steps as a workflow, so the next AI finds it (find_workflow) and runs it instead of working it out again.
words.improved_note: This run improved a workflow Trillion had already learned; its earlier versions are kept in its versions.
words.same_note: This run followed a workflow Trillion had already learned, so nothing changed.
words.shared_note: It is shared into {spaces}, so the people there and their AIs have it now.
words.retry_job:
This job stopped before it was done. Get it done: {job}
Where the last attempt stopped: {wall}
words.retry_outcome: The job's result exists and is checked.
words.retry_note: The job stopped without its result, so it was handed on as open work ({handoff_id}) with the exact wall.
words.shape_step_do: Trillion runs {tool_id} for this step with the values the workflow was started with (or an earlier step's result); nothing to do here but read the run.
words.shape_published_note: Its steps, without anything of this job's own, are on the Marketplace as {workflow_id}, so any AI finds and runs it.
words.shape_same_note: The same steps are already on the Marketplace as {workflow_id}.
words.refused_few_runs: Fewer than {min} tools ran and finished, so there is nothing to share.
words.refused_unknown_tool: {tool_id} could not be read, so whether other accounts can run it is unknown.
words.refused_own_tool: {tool_id} is a tool only this account has; publish it first (publish_tool) so other accounts can run these steps.
words.refused_output_shape: {tool_id} hands back something other than an object, so a later step cannot read its result.
words.refused_private_value: A value this job ran with would appear in the shared steps.
words.refused_secret: Something shaped like a key or token would appear in the shared steps.
words.refused_duplicate: {workflow_id} already runs these same tools in this order; it is used instead of a second copy.
